items.answer: oxygen gas

items.stem: Classify these as a part of the biosphere or a part of the hydrosphere: a peepal tree, earthworms in the soil, groundwater, fish in a river, the Arabian Sea.
items.answer: A part of the biosphere: a peepal tree, earthworms in the soil, fish in a river. A part of the hydrosphere: groundwater, the Arabian Sea.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a part of the hydrosphere?
items.answer: the ozone layer
items.markingKey: (a) The ozone layer is a part of the atmosphere, not a part of the hydrosphere. Each of the others (glaciers of the Himalayas, groundwater, Chilika lake) is a part of the hydrosphere.

items.stem: Explain with one example each how the four spheres interact during the formation of rain.
items.answer: Water evaporates from the hydrosphere (sea) into the atmosphere, condenses into clouds and falls on the lithosphere; plants (biosphere) add water by transpiration and use rain to grow.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per sphere (any three).

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The solid outer layer of the Earth made of rocks and soil."
items.answer: the lithosphere
items.markingKey: (c) The lithosphere is the solid outer layer of the Earth made of rocks and soil.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a part of the atmosphere?
items.answer: sand on a beach
items.markingKey: (b) Sand on a beach is a part of the lithosphere, not a part of the atmosphere. Each of the others (oxygen gas, the ozone layer, carbon dioxide gas) is a part of the atmosphere.

items.stem: Which of the following is a part of the biosphere?
items.answer: fish in a river
items.markingKey: (c) Fish in a river is a part of the biosphere. The others: the Deccan plateau – a part of the lithosphere; the ozone layer – a part of the atmosphere; groundwater – a part of the hydrosphere.

items.stem: Classify these as a part of the lithosphere or a part of the atmosphere: soil in a field, the Deccan plateau, carbon dioxide gas, granite rock.

items.stem: Define the hydrosphere.
items.answer: All the water on the Earth, in oceans, rivers, lakes, ice and underground
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The hydrosphere – all the water on the Earth, in oceans, rivers, lakes, ice and underground.

items.stem: How are lichens and mosses involved in soil formation?
items.answer: Lichens release substances that powder the rock surface, and mosses then grow and break the rock further.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Which of these increases the carbon dioxide level in air?
items.answer: burning of fossil fuels

items.stem: Which of these removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
items.answer: dissolving in sea water
items.markingKey: (a) Dissolving in sea water — removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. items.stem: How does transpiration take part in the water cycle?
items.answer: Plants absorb water from the soil and release it as water vapour from their leaves; the vapour condenses into clouds.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: absorb and release. 1 mark: forms clouds.

items.stem: Arrange these steps of the water cycle in the correct order: (1) water flows into rivers or seeps into groundwater; (2) water vapour rises and cools; (3) water falls as rain or snow; (4) it condenses into clouds; (5) it returns to the sea.
items.markingKey: Correct order: water vapour rises and cools → it condenses into clouds → water falls as rain or snow → water flows into rivers or seeps into groundwater → it returns to the sea.

items.stem: Arjun's father drives 20 km a day for 25 days a month in Lucknow. If his car emits 150 g of CO₂ per km, how much CO₂ does it give out in a month, and in a year? About how many trees would be needed to absorb a year's emission if one tree absorbs 22 kg a year?
items.answer: 75 kg a month; 900 kg a year; at least 41 trees.
items.markingKey: Month: 20 × 25 × 150 g = 75 kg. Year: × 12 = 900 kg. Trees: 900/22 ≈ 40.9, so at least 41 trees.

items.stem: Why does the carbon dioxide level rise in cities in winter evenings, and how can trees in parks help?
items.answer: More fuel is burnt for heating and traffic, and still, cold air traps pollutants near the ground; trees absorb CO₂ by photosynthesis in the day and trap dust.
items.markingKey: 1 mark cause. 1 mark trapping. 1 mark trees.

items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Part of the oxygen cycle: use of O₂ in combustion. Part of the water cycle: condensation in clouds; evaporation from the sea; precipitation as rain.

items.stem: Describe the carbon cycle and the oxygen cycle. How do human activities disturb them, and what are the consequences?
items.answer: Carbon: CO₂ taken up in photosynthesis, passed along food chains, returned by respiration, decomposition and combustion; also stored in carbonates and fossil fuels. Oxygen: released in photosynthesis, used in respiration, combustion and formation of oxides. Humans burn fossil fuels and cut forests, raising CO₂: greenhouse effect, global warming, melting glaciers, rise in sea level.
items.markingKey: 2 marks carbon; 1 mark oxygen; 2 marks disturbance and effects.

items.stem: Arrange these steps of the water cycle in the correct order: (1) water vapour rises and cools; (2) it condenses into clouds; (3) it returns to the sea; (4) water flows into rivers or seeps into groundwater; (5) water evaporates from the sea and water bodies; (6) water falls as rain or snow.

items.stem: How does deforestation lead to soil erosion?
items.answer: Roots of trees hold the soil; without trees, rain and wind easily wash or blow away the fertile topsoil.

items.stem:
Read: Farmers in Punjab burn rice stubble in October. Within days the AQI in Delhi rises above 400, schools are closed and many people complain of breathlessness.
(i) Name two pollutants released by burning stubble. (ii) Why do people feel breathless? (iii) How does burning harm the soil? (iv) Suggest one alternative to burning.
items.answer: (i) Fine particles (smoke), carbon monoxide, oxides of nitrogen. (ii) Fine particles and gases damage the lungs and reduce oxygen supply. (iii) It kills useful soil microbes and destroys nutrients. (iv) Use Happy Seeder machines, decompose stubble with bio-decomposer sprays, or use it as cattle feed/fuel pellets.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: A town near a river has a sugar mill that discharges hot waste water and a nearby farm that uses heavy fertilisers. Fish in the river are dying. Give two causes and suggest two remedies.

items.stem: Sahil's father drives 50 km a day for 25 days a month in Lucknow. If his car emits 180 g of CO₂ per km, how much CO₂ does it give out in a month, and in a year? About how many trees would be needed to absorb a year's emission if one tree absorbs 22 kg a year?
items.answer: 225 kg a month; 2700 kg a year; at least 123 trees.
items.markingKey: Month: 50 × 25 × 180 g = 225 kg. Year: × 12 = 2700 kg. Trees: 2700/22 ≈ 122.7, so at least 123 trees.

items.stem: Why is the oxygen content of the air almost constant even though it is used up in respiration and burning?
